title: Real Vista documentation
text: What it is Real Vista is a SaaS CRM for real estate agencies. One deployment serves many agencies; each agency gets an isolated workspace with its own users, properties, leads, branding and pipeline. Agency staff (admins and employees) work in the CRM; sellers use a lighter surface; people outside the agency see only what is deliberately shared with them through expiring links. Getting started Run it locally and create your first workspace. Product guide Leads, pipeline, listings, sharing, roles and settings. Architecture How the pieces fit, and the rules that keep them safe. Multi-tenancy Isolation, platform operators, plans and billing. API reference Every endpoint, generated from the code. Operations Deploy, back up, monitor, recover. The shape of the system React + Vite app (CRM, public pages) Express API (port 3000) MongoDB (one DB, tenantId on every document) Flutter mobile app Same API + Cloudinary (media, from the browser) + Socket.IO (realtime) Principles you will meet everywhere Principle In practice Isolation is enforced in the data layer A global Mongoose plugin scopes every query to one workspace. A query with no tenant context throws rather than returning someone else's records. Details Vocabulary in code, selection in config Permissions, notification types, webhook events, rules, pipeline stages and screens are fixed catalogues in one file each; a workspace chooses from them and never supplies code. The property book is private Nothing about a listing is reachable without a session. Sharing goes through expiring, revocable links. Sharing One error shape Every failure is { success:false, statusCode, code, message, requestId } . Branch on code . Pipeline Claims match code Public pages carry no invented statistics, and policy text changes with the behaviour it describes. Who should read what If you are Start with A new developer Getting started , then Architecture and Multi-tenancy , and CLAUDE.md at the repo root for the rules that came from real bugs. An agency admin Team, roles and permissions and Workspace settings . An agent Leads and pipeline and Listings and categories . Integrating with the API API conventions and the reference . Running a deployment Deploy and operate and the FAQ . Keeping these docs true The API reference is generated: npm run docs:openapi rewrites docs/openapi.json from the live router, then npm run docs:site rebuilds this site into docs/site . Pages are fragments in docs/site-src/pages . The build fails on a navigation entry with no page and on a broken internal link. When a change alters behaviour a page describes, change the page in the same commit.

title: Getting started
headings: Create your first workspace and admin
text: Prerequisites Tool Notes Node.js 20 CI ( .github/workflows/ci.yml ) runs on Node 20 and neither package.json declares an engines field. Run the backend on Node 20: on Node 25 the jsonwebtoken dependency chain ( jwa / buffer-equal-constant-time ) uses the removed SlowBuffer API and crashes on require. The Vite frontend ran fine on Node 25 in our tests. MongoDB A local mongod is the simplest option. The default MONGO_URI used in docs and the example file is mongodb://127.0.0.1:27017/mern-estate . The unit tests do not need it (they start an in-memory server, see Running tests ). npm Each of backend/ , frontend/ and the repo root has its own package.json and lock file. Redis (optional) Only needed when you run more than one backend instance. See REDIS_URL below. Cloudinary account (optional) Listing photos and voice notes are uploaded from the browser straight to Cloudinary. Without it the rest of the app works but those uploads do not. macOS note: mongod --fork is not supported there. Start it in the foreground or via a service, e.g. mongod --config /opt/homebrew/etc/mongod.conf for a Homebrew install. Clone and install git clone repo-url mern-estate cd mern-estate/backend npm install cd ../frontend npm install cd .. npm install # repo root: Playwright e2e only If npm install fails with a 401 on package fetches, your user-level ~/.npmrc may point at a private registry. Override per command: npm_config_registry=https://registry.npmjs.org npm install . Backend environment Copy backend/.env.example to backend/.env . backend/config/environment.js loads it and exits the process if any of these five are missing: JWT_SECRET , REFRESH_SECRET , MONGO_URI , NODE_ENV , MESSAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY . validateConfig() additionally requires both JWT secrets to be at least 32 characters, and in production requires APP_DOMAIN or DEFAULT_TENANT_SLUG . Generate secrets with node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(64).toString('hex'))" (the example file uses 32 bytes for MESSAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY ). Variable Required Default Purpose NODE_ENV yes none development , production or test . Production tightens CORS and config validation. MONGO_URI yes none MongoDB connection string. JWT_SECRET yes none Signs access tokens; at least 32 characters. REFRESH_SECRET yes none Signs refresh tokens; at least 32 characters. MESSAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY yes none Key for chat message encryption. Without it the first socket message would throw, so it is checked at boot. PORT no 3000 API port. The Vite proxy targets 3000. HOST no 0.0.0.0 Bind address. ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRY / REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRY no 15m / 30d Token lifetimes. JWT_ISSUER / JWT_AUDIENCE no mern-estate-api / mern-estate-client Token claims. DEFAULT_TENANT_SLUG production: one of this or APP_DOMAIN default Workspace a request falls back to when nothing else identifies one. APP_DOMAIN no empty Enables subdomain routing: acme. APP_DOMAIN resolves to the workspace with slug acme . FRONTEND_URL , ADMIN_URL production (warning only) none Production CORS origins and the base of links in invite and reset emails. EXTRA_CORS_ORIGINS no none Comma-separated extra origins allowed in development (for example a Flutter web dev port). DB_MAX_POOL_SIZE , DB_SERVER_SELECTION_TIMEOUT , DB_SOCKET_TIMEOUT no 10 , 5000 , 45000 Mongo driver options (ms for timeouts). MAX_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS , LOCKOUT_DURATION no 5 , 15 minutes (ms) Account lockout. ENABLE_RATE_LIMITING no on (anything but false ) Rate limiter switch. RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS , RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS , AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX , STRICT_RATE_LIMIT_MAX no 15 min, 1000 , 20 , 30 Limiter windows and ceilings. SMTP_HOST , SMTP_USER , SMTP_PASS no none Outgoing mail (password reset, invites, notifications, sequences). Production logs a warning when unset and mail features are disabled. .env.example also lists SMTP_PORT , SMTP_SECURE , EMAIL_FROM . TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID , TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN , TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER no none SMS. CACHE_TTL , CACHE_MAX_SIZE no 300 s, 100 In-process response cache. REDIS_URL no none Makes the rate limiter and cache invalidation shared across instances. JOBS_ENABLED no on Set false on an instance that should serve traffic but take no scheduled-job leases. OPENOBSERVE_URL , OPENOBSERVE_ORG , OPENOBSERVE_USERNAME , OPENOBSERVE_PASSWORD no none Log shipping. With no username/password, logs go to stdout only. ENCRYPT_API_RESPONSES , API_RESPONSE_SECRET no off Encrypts API responses; the secret must then be set and match the frontend's VITE_API_RESPONSE_SECRET . UNSUBSCRIBE_SECRET , PUBLIC_API_URL no derived from JWT_SECRET Signs unsubscribe links in automated emails (never rotate once mail has gone out); PUBLIC_API_URL is for split deployments. METRICS_TOKEN , SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS , NOTIFY_TO , PUBLIC_BASE_URL no none Read in code ( grep process.env backend ) but not in .env.example . BACKUP_DIR , BACKUP_RETENTION_COUNT , ALLOW_PRODUCTION_RESTORE no ../backups relative to scripts/ Used by db:backup / db:restore . Several keys in .env.example (for example BCRYPT_ROUNDS , SESSION_TIMEOUT , PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH , ENABLE_SWAGGER , SENTRY_DSN ) are not read by any file under backend/ outside tests; the file itself says SENTRY_DSN is read by nothing. Treat the table above, which is derived from process.env usage, as the working set. Frontend environment Copy frontend/.env.example to frontend/.env.local . All variables must start with VITE_ and are baked into the bundle at build time, so none of them is a secret. Variable Required Purpose VITE_API_URL no Empty in development (the Vite proxy forwards /api and /uploads to http://localhost:3000 ). Set it in production when the API is on another origin. VITE_SOCKET_URL no Socket.IO origin. Empty falls back to localhost:3000 in dev and same origin in production. VITE_CLOUDINARY_CLOUD_NAME , VITE_CLOUDINARY_UPLOAD_PRESET for photo and voice-note upload Use an unsigned upload preset. VITE_API_RESPONSE_SECRET only if responses are encrypted Must equal the backend API_RESPONSE_SECRET . VITE_SENTR

title: Leads and pipeline
headings: Quick reference: who can do what
text: Who is who Three kinds of people live in three different screens. Mixing them up is the most common mistake. Concept Screen (default label) Route What it is Lead / client Clients /clients , /clients/:id A sales lead: someone who may buy or rent. The Client model; each has a status, priority, source, budget, score, deals, follow-ups and a communications log. A "contact type" marks it as lead , co_agent or referral_partner . Owner Property Owners /owners A landlord or seller whose property you list. Name, contact details, company, address, optional tax id (hidden from normal reads), active flag. Not a sales lead. Buyer requirement Buyer Requirements /buyers What one buyer wants (sale or rent, price range, bedrooms, bathrooms, location), matched against your stock. A workspace may rename any screen under Settings (for example "Clients" to "Leads"); the sidebar then shows the workspace's label. See Workspace settings . The old paths /contacts , /deals , /buyer-requirements and /client-reports still work as aliases of /owners , /pipeline , /buyers and /reports . Lead created → Assigned → Calls, notes, follow-ups → Deal on the pipeline → Won or Lost Who sees which leads An admin sees every lead in the workspace and may filter by agent. An employee sees and edits only leads assigned to them, whatever the query string says. This holds for the list, export, bulk actions, pipeline, bottlenecks, follow-ups, ROI report and sequences. On top of that, the Clients endpoints need a permission: viewClients , createClient , updateClient , deleteClient , exportData . Admins pass every permission check; an employee needs a custom role that grants them (an employee with no role gets "No role assigned"). See Team, roles and permissions . The CRM endpoints ( /api/crm/* : deals, follow-ups, communications, summary, pipeline) check only that the caller is an admin or employee and, for single-lead calls, that the lead is theirs. They do not check a permission key. Create and find leads To add a lead: Clients, then New client (the command palette's "New client" opens the same form via /clients?new=1 ). Requires createClient . Only the name is required by the model. Duplicates are refused. The server looks across the whole workspace (not just your leads) for the same email, or for the same phone using the last ten digits (so "+91 98765 43210" and "09876543210" match). A hit answers 409 with the existing lead's name, owner and status. The API accepts ?force=true to create anyway; the Clients form has no override button, so use the existing record or the API. Who owns it. If you name no owner, the workspace's lead-assignment rule picks one (see Assignment ). An employee cannot assign a lead to anyone but themselves. The score is calculated at creation, so a new lead with a budget and an urgent priority does not start cold. The list has three views: Cards , Board and Table . Filters: search text, status, contact type, owner (admin), tag and temperature. The table sorts and pages on the server (sortable: name, score, temperature, status, priority, budget, next follow-up, email, created, updated). Export downloads a CSV of everything matching the current filters (not just the page; capped at 50,000 rows) and needs exportData . Lead status and priority Field Values status lead (default), contacted , qualified , proposal , negotiation , won , lost priority low , medium (default), high , urgent temperature hot , warm , cold (default) Bulk actions Tick rows, then use the bar: assign (admin only), change status , delete , and tag or untag (API actions assign , status , delete , tag , untag ). Up to 500 ids at once. Requires updateClient . An employee's selection is narrowed to the leads they own before anything is written; ids they do not own are silently skipped. Deleting a lead is a soft delete. Lead score and temperature client.calculateScore() is the only place the score is computed. It adds five factors and caps the total at 100: Factor Points Engagement 10 per communication logged in the last 30 days, max 30 Budget 20 if a maximum budget is set, otherwise 0 Urgency by priority: low 5, medium 10, high 20, urgent 30 Fit 5 per interested listing, max 20 Recency by days since last contact (or last update): 7 or fewer 20; up to 30 days 12; up to 90 days 5; beyond that 0 Temperature follows the score: 60 and above is hot , 30 and above is warm , below that cold . The score is recomputed when a lead is created, when it is edited, when a communication is logged, edited or deleted, when a deal changes stage, and nightly at 03:00 (UTC, job lead-rescore ), because the recency factor decays with time. Manual temperature is pinned. If you choose Hot, Warm or Cold on the lead's Overview (the Temperature control says "Set by hand — the nightly score will not change it"), the server sets temperatureManual and stops deriving temperature from the score. The score itself keeps updating. The code has no endpoint or button that clears temperatureManual again; only a direct database edit does. Won and lost leads are never rescored by the nightly job , so past reports do not change. (The job also processes at most 1,000 open leads per workspace per run, in natural order, because rescoreLeads takes a batch of 1,000 with no cursor. A workspace with more open leads than that will not have every lead refreshed nightly.) Working a lead Open a lead from Clients ( /clients/:id ). The header shows Active Deals, Won Value, Pending Follow-ups and Lead Score. Tabs: Overview , Deals , Follow-ups , Timeline , Calls/Notes , Tasks , Documents . Overview Contact information, source, requirements (budget range, property type, preferred locations, free text) with inline edit, and tags (see Tags ). Temperature control (above). Assigned to and, for an admin, a "Reassign to" picker listing active admins and employees. Reassigning asks for confirmation when the lead already has an owner. title: Listings and categories
headings: Things the form does for you
Destructive actions answer 409 with a count
text: The property book A listing is one property. Properties are grouped into categories (a colony, a project, "Apartments"), and a category decides which extra fields a property in it collects. The register is the All Properties screen ( /properties ); the form is /create-listing and /update-listing/:listingId . Nothing about a listing, category or property type is reachable without a signed-in session; to show a property to someone outside the agency use a share link, see Sharing and imports . Add or edit a property To add a property: sidebar, Add Property (needs createListing ; employees with no custom role may also create, subject to category assignment). To edit: open the property and choose edit. Both use the same form ( pages/ListingForm.jsx ); the only difference is that Documents and Voice notes appear only once the property exists. Section Contents The property Name (the only always-required field), category, property type, listing type (for sale, for rent, for lease), status, property or plot number, description. Where it is Address, area or colony, locality or sector, city, state, pincode, and a map pin. Type an address and use Find on map , or click the map. Price and size Price, offer price, bedrooms, bathrooms, area, plot size, square-yard figures, total value. Amounts use the workspace currency and area unit. Category details The category's own fields (below). Fields marked * are required. Photos The first photo is the one used everywhere else in the product. Images upload from the browser straight to Cloudinary. Owners One or more Property Owners; you can create an owner inline. Internal notes Visible to your team only. Documents, Voice notes Edit mode only. Statuses and types Field Values status available (default), sold , rented , under_negotiation type sale (default), rent , lease propertyCategory residential , commercial , land , industrial , other , unknown (default). Inferred from the property type when you do not set it. A listing's status also changes by itself: when a deal is marked Won on a lead, the linked listing becomes sold (or rented for a rent or lease deal). See Deals . Things the form does for you Unsaved changes are tracked against what was loaded. Edit conflicts. The form remembers the updatedAt it loaded and sends it back as expectedUpdatedAt . If a colleague saved first the server answers 409 VERSION_CONFLICT and the form shows a notice with Load their version or Keep mine (which resends without the guard). A caller that sends no version (scripts, the mobile app) gets last-write-wins. Find on map fills only empty fields, so a typed address is not overwritten by the geocoder's best match, but the map pin itself is always updated. Category fields whose key is a real column (bedrooms, bathrooms, parking, furnishing) are copied into that column too, because filters, cards and the bed/bath line read the column. What gates it Plan limit maxListings (trial 250, starter 2,500, growth 25,000, enterprise unlimited). Creating over the cap answers 402. Bulk import checks the number it is about to create before writing any row. Employees can create a listing only in a category assigned to them (otherwise "Not allowed for this category"), and can edit or delete only listings they created, are assigned to, or that sit in their assigned categories. Sellers see only their own listings. See employee scoping . Buyers cannot create, update or delete listings. A workspace rule can normalise or veto a save (for example refuse to save without a price); the user sees the rule's message. Deleting and restoring Deleting a listing is always a soft delete ( isDeleted , deletedAt ). Removing a property from the board hides it from search, facets and lists but does not destroy it. To delete: from the board or the property. Anyone who can access the listing can delete it through DELETE /api/listing/delete/:id ; admins also have POST /api/listing/soft-delete/:id . To restore: admin only. On All Properties open the bin (the Deleted listings dialog) and restore; it lists up to 200, newest deleted first. Restoring does not re-check the plan's maxListings cap; the cap is enforced when listings are created or imported, not when they are un-deleted. The All Properties board The same data in four views, chosen with ?view= in the URL: Main table (default), Pipeline (by status), Cards and Map . The table sorts and pages on the server. Filters, all kept in the URL so a view is linkable: search text, status, assigned agent, owner, city, locality, listing type, category, property category, property type, min and max price, minimum bedrooms and bathrooms, furnished, parking and offer. Saved views (the bar above the table) store the current filter query string under a name. They belong to the signed-in user, follow them across devices ( /api/user/saved-views/:namespace ), and hold up to 50 per list. Views saved by older versions in the browser are merged up once. Assigning an agent to a listing is admin-only ( POST /api/listing/assign-agent and /unassign-agent ). The assigned agent gains edit access, and "My assigned" lists their listings. Search There is one listing search, backend/search/listingSearch.js , used by the board, the search page and the command palette. It scopes results to what the signed-in user may see, then matches in tiers and stops once there are enough results: Identifier : property number, pincode or id, exact. Text : the database text index, ranked by relevance. Prefix : an anchored prefix on city, locality, area name or name ("Sush" finds "Sushant"). Fuzzy : a looser pattern, only against a set the filters have already narrowed. Ranking and paging happen in the database, so the total is the real number of matches and any page can be fetched. Facet counts. GET /api/listing/facets returns counts by status, category, city, locality, type and assigned agent (top 50 for the open-ended ones) plus total count, total value and average price over the whole filtered set. title: Sharing and imports
text: Share links Nothing about a listing is reachable without a session, so a share link is the only way a property leaves the agency. An agent picks properties, gets a link and sends it (for example on WhatsApp). The recipient opens /s/:token with no account. The token is the credential. Anyone holding the link can open it until it expires or is withdrawn. Treat a link like a password: send it only to the intended person, prefer an expiry, and add a passcode for anything sensitive. Create a link To share: on All Properties select one or more rows and choose Share, or use Share on a single property's page. Fill in: Field Behaviour What is this list? A label so your list of links is readable (up to 120 characters). Sent to, their phone A note to yourself. Never shown on the shared page. Message Up to 1,000 characters, shown at the top of the shared page. Link expires in 7, 30 (default), 90 days or No expiry . The API accepts 1 to 365 days; null means no expiry and is a deliberate choice. Passcode Optional, at least 4 characters. Stored hashed (bcrypt). The recipient is asked for it before anything is returned. Show the price On by default. Off withholds price, offer price and the offer flag from the page, for gauging interest before a number is agreed. A link carries between 1 and 50 properties. The token is 32 random bytes (base64url), so it cannot be guessed. You cannot share what you cannot see. The server re-reads the chosen properties through your own access scope ( listingScope ). If any are outside it, the whole request is refused with "Some of those properties are not yours to share". An employee can share only listings they created, are assigned to, or that sit in their assigned categories; sellers only their own. There is no separate permission key for sharing; any signed-in user passes this check for properties in scope. Track and revoke The Share links dialog on All Properties lists links with their state, view count and last-viewed time. An admin sees every link in the workspace (latest 200); anyone else sees their own. To withdraw a link: Revoke. It sets revokedAt and revokedBy instead of deleting, so "who did we send this to and when did we stop it" stays answerable. Only the creator or an admin can revoke, and a link already withdrawn cannot be revoked again. Every successful open increments the view count; a count that climbs unexpectedly means the link has spread. What the recipient sees GET /api/share/open/:token is the one unauthenticated endpoint that returns property data. It is rate-limited to 60 requests per 15 minutes. The workspace comes from the share record, so a token reaches only the workspace that issued it. Situation Response Token does not exist 404 "This link is not valid." (the same answer for old and never-existing tokens, so valid tokens cannot be enumerated) Revoked 410 "This link has been withdrawn by the agent." Expired 410 "This link has expired." Passcode required, none sent 401 with passcodeRequired: true ; the page shows a passcode prompt. The browser sends it in the x-share-passcode header. Wrong passcode 401 "That passcode is not right." and a security log line forRecipient() is an allowlist , so a new Listing column never becomes public by being added. The page shows only: name, description, address, area name, locality, city, state, type, status, bedrooms, bathrooms, area (sq ft), sq yard, plot size, furnished, parking, photos, map location and, unless hidden, regular price, offer price and the offer flag. It never includes owners or owner contacts, the assigned agent, the creator, internal notes ( remarks ), voice notes, category attributes, cost or commission fields or the tenant id. The page is dressed in the agency's name, logo, brand colours and support email and phone. Imports: shared rules Both importers (properties and leads) follow the same pattern: Choose file → Match columns → Preview (writes nothing) → Commit in batches Every row is validated before anything is written. Preview and commit build rows through the same code, so the report you approve is what lands. Rows are written in batches with per-row results, so one bad row costs that row and not the file. Row problems are returned individually and capped (see each importer). Files: .xlsx , .xls or .csv , up to 15 MB (the browser rejects larger files and unsupported types before upload). Monthly import meter. The plan limit maxImportRowsPerMonth counts rows brought in by either importer (trial 2,000, starter 20,000, growth 100,000, enterprise unlimited). Rows are reserved before writing and the unused part is released, so rejected rows cost nothing. If the file would pass the cap the request answers 402 with details.limit , used , requested and remaining . The counter resets at the start of each month in the workspace's timezone (a daily job rolls it). Import properties To import: Import from Excel in the sidebar, the Import button on Categories, or /admin/import . Admin only (the screen is adminOnly and every route is requireAdmin ); it is a screen a workspace can switch off. Choose file. Pick the category first: its fields decide what columns are understood. Download a template CSV for that category ( GET /api/listing/import/template ) to skip the mapping step entirely. Match columns. Headers are auto-mapped using synonyms (for example "plot no", "unit number" and "khasra no" map to Property / plot no.; "bhk" to Bedrooms; "gaj" to sq. yard). Each column can be sent to a core field, a category field or ignored. Prices accept forms like "1.4 Cr". Review. Preview classifies each row as ready , error , duplicate (already in the system) or duplicate_in_file (an earlier row in the same file is the same property). Pick what to do with existing duplicates: Leave the existing one alone ( skip , default; safest for topping up a list); Update it with this row ( update ; overwrites the existing property); Add it anyway ( create ; a second record). title: Team, roles and permissions
text: Two layers of access What a person can do is decided by two separate things. Mixing them up is the most common source of "why can't they see it". Account type ( user.role ): admin , employee , seller , buyer (the schema also allows user , the default). Only admin and employee can enter the CRM (the CRM shell requires one of the two). Custom role ( user.assignedRole ): a named bundle of permissions that you assign to an employee . Admins bypass permission checks entirely. Then a third thing narrows the data: scoping (which categories, listings and leads an employee may touch). Account type What it means admin Admin of one workspace , not the vendor. Sees everything in that workspace, passes every permission check, manages users, roles and settings. Not the same as a platform operator (see Multi-tenancy ). employee Agency staff. Gets only the permissions of the custom role assigned to them, and sees only data in their scope. seller Sees only listings they created. No CRM. buyer No CRM; may not create, edit or delete listings. An employee with no custom role can do almost nothing. The permission check answers 403 "No role assigned. Access denied." and the app's permission context resolves to an empty set, so the CRM screens redirect to "Unauthorized". The single exception is creating listings, which an employee with no role is allowed (category restrictions still apply). Always assign a role right after inviting an employee. Add a team member To invite an employee: Admin Panel ( /admin ), Users tab, Create Employee : username, email, optional phone, and the categories they are assigned to. Admin only. Then assign a role in the Roles Permissions tab. Counts against the plan's seat limit maxUsers (trial 3, starter 10, growth 40, enterprise unlimited). At the cap the request answers 402 before anything is created. Email must be unused in the workspace (409 otherwise); a phone number must also be unused. No password is ever chosen or emailed. The account is created with a random password nobody sees, and an invitation is sent. Invitations The invite email links to /invite/:token . The token is 32 random bytes, stored only as a SHA-256 hash, valid for 7 days and single-use . The link carries the workspace, so the recipient lands in the right agency without knowing the word "workspace". The invitee chooses a password and must accept the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. The acceptance records the legal version and time. They are then signed in directly, and the email tells them the workspace address to use on later sign-ins. An unknown, expired or already-used token all show the same "no longer valid" message, so tokens cannot be probed. Only the newest invitation works. Sending a fresh invite remembers up to four earlier links; opening one of those answers 410 with code INVITE_REPLACED ("A newer invitation was sent to you") so the invitee knows to open the newer email. If mail is not configured the invite cannot be delivered. The create call returns the link ( inviteUrl ) so an admin could pass it on, but the Admin Panel does not display it, and there is no tenant-admin button to re-send an employee invite (the platform console can re-send a workspace's first admin invite only). To unblock someone, an admin can set an employee's password directly (below). Manage existing users In the Users tab, open Manage on a person. All of these are admin-only and refuse to act on yourself or on another admin: Action Rules Change account type and assigned categories POST /api/user/role/:id . You cannot change your own type or another admin's. Deactivate or reactivate Status active / inactive . An inactive account cannot sign in ("Your account is inactive"). Not allowed on admins or yourself. Set an employee's password Employees only (not admins, not yourself). The password must meet the rules below. It clears pending reset codes and signs the employee out everywhere (refresh tokens are cleared). A security-log entry admin_password_reset is written. Delete Soft delete, not on admins or yourself. A person can close their own account from Settings, Privacy (Close Account) or their Profile; that erases their personal details and keeps the records they created, attributed to "Former team member". See Data rights . Password rules and lockout At least 8 characters with an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a digit and a special character from ! @ # $ % ^ * ( ) , . ? " : { } | . The same check applies to invites, password changes, resets and admin resets. After 5 failed sign-ins ( MAX_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS ) the account is locked for 15 minutes ( LOCKOUT_DURATION ); a successful sign-in resets the counter. Auth endpoints are rate-limited (20 requests per 15 minutes by default in production). Sessions: 15-minute access token and 30-day refresh token in httpOnly cookies. See Authentication . Custom roles Roles live under Admin Panel, Roles Permissions ( RoleManagement ). The whole /api/roles API is admin-only, whatever the manageRoles permission says. Create a role: a unique name (per workspace), a description (up to 500 characters) and ticked permissions. All permissions default to off. Assign / remove: choose a role for a user ( POST /api/roles/assign , /remove ). You cannot assign an inactive role. Members: open a role to list its members ( GET /api/roles/:id/users ). Edit: a role marked isSystem cannot be renamed or deactivated; its permissions can still be edited. Delete: system roles cannot be deleted. A role with members answers 400 "Cannot delete role. N user(s) are assigned…"; confirming a force delete ( ?force=true ) unassigns everyone and then soft-deletes the role. Those employees are left with no role, which locks them out of most of the CRM (see the warning above). Restore default roles: the button calls GET /api/roles/initialize-defaults (a GET that writes), which creates any of the three built-in roles that do not already exist by name and leaves existing ones untouched. title: System architecture
text: The shape of the system The repository is one monorepo with a Node/Express API, a React single-page app and a Flutter mobile app. One deployment serves many agencies ( tenants ) from a single MongoDB database. Everything else on this page follows from that decision, so read Multi-tenancy and platform admin alongside it. / ├── backend/ Node/Express API (default port 3000) │ ├── app.js createApp(): middleware order, route mounting, 404s, error handler │ ├── index.js process entry: tenancy registration, boot, ordered shutdown │ ├── server.js HTTP server, DB connect, Socket.IO event handlers │ ├── socket.js Socket.IO auth handshake, emitToTenant / emitToUser │ ├── config/ environment.js (config + validateConfig), database.js │ ├── controllers/ request handlers (one file per area) │ ├── routes/ Express routers (one file per mount point) │ ├── middleware/ security, csrf, validation, permissions, errorEnvelope, ... │ ├── models/ Mongoose models (36) │ ├── tenancy/ tenant plugin, context, resolution, plans, limits, billing │ ├── jobs/ scheduler and the scheduled jobs │ ├── plugins/ workspace rule registry and built-in rules │ ├── search/ the one listing search, the parser, per-entity searchers │ ├── security/ publicRoutes.js - the allowlist of unauthenticated routes │ ├── utils/ error, cache, notify, webhooks, logger, openapi, ... │ ├── scripts/ CLI: provisioning, seeds, backup/restore, migrations │ └── tests/ Jest suites (including the structural ones) ├── frontend/ React + Vite (dev server on 5173, proxies /api and /uploads) │ └── src/ app/ (routes, shells), components/, design-system/, hooks/, │ i18n/, pages/, redux/, utils/ (http.js, cloudinary.js, currency.js) ├── mobile/ Flutter app └── docs/ openapi.json (generated) and this site (docs/site-src) Two long-standing sentences in CLAUDE.md are slightly stale: the auth middleware is not in backend/middleware/auth.js (that file does not exist; verifyToken , tryVerifyToken , requireAdmin and requireRole live in backend/utils/verifyUser.js ), and the required environment variables are wider than four (see Configuration ). A request, end to end Browser / app → security + parsing + rate limit → resolveTenant → CSRF, auth guard, validateBody → controller (queries auto-scoped) → JSON envelope The exact order, and why it matters, is in Request pipeline and errors . The short version: everything after resolveTenant runs inside an AsyncLocalStorage tenant context, so every Mongoose query is filtered by tenantId without any controller asking for it. Startup sequence ( backend/index.js ) Register tenancy first. registerTenancy(mongoose) installs the global tenant plugin. A Mongoose global plugin only applies to schemas compiled after it is registered, and ES imports are hoisted, so index.js deliberately uses await import('./server.js') after registering. Importing any model before this line would produce a model with no tenantId . validateConfig() checks secrets and production settings (see Configuration ) and exits on error. registerBuiltinRules() fills the workspace rule vocabulary, because rules are resolved by name and must exist before the first request can run a hook. startCacheInvalidationListener() subscribes to Redis when REDIS_URL is set; otherwise it is a no-op. setupSocket() attaches the Socket.IO connection handlers, then startServer() connects to Mongo, seeds default property types for any workspace that has none, and listens. startJobs() runs after the server is listening, so a job failure cannot stop boot. JOBS_ENABLED=false skips it (see Background jobs ). Shutdown sequence There is exactly one shutdown path, shutdown(reason, exitCode) in index.js , bound to SIGTERM , SIGINT , unhandledRejection and uncaughtException . Never add another SIGTERM handler. The pieces used to race: the database module exited the instant Mongo disconnected, so in-flight requests got a reset connection, the logger's flush lost, and the scheduler's lease was never released. markShuttingDown() ( utils/lifecycle.js ) makes GET /api/health/ready answer 503 so a load balancer stops sending traffic. Stop accepting connections and wait for in-flight requests ( server.close , plus closeIdleConnections so keep-alive sockets do not hold it open). stopScheduler() and stopCacheInvalidationListener() . Close Socket.IO, Redis, and the Mongo connection. flushLogs() , then process.exit . SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS (default 10000) bounds the wait; after it, remaining connections are closed forcibly. backend/ecosystem.config.js sets PM2 kill_timeout: 5000 , shorter than the 10 s default drain, and wait_ready: true although nothing in the backend calls process.send('ready') (PM2 then falls back to listen_timeout ). If you rely on PM2 for graceful drains, raise kill_timeout above SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS . Configuration backend/config/environment.js loads backend/.env and exits immediately if any of these are missing: JWT_SECRET , REFRESH_SECRET , MONGO_URI , NODE_ENV , MESSAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY . The last one is required because without it the first Socket.IO message send would throw inside an unhandled-rejection handler and take the server down. title: Multi-tenancy and platform admin
headings: The model: shared database, one tenantId per document
How a request picks its workspace
Acting as a customer: identity is pinned, data is not
Every query about the caller must be pinned
Billing is a ledger, not a gateway
Anything outside the database needs its own tenant boundary
text: The model: shared database, one tenantId per document A tenant (also called a workspace) is one real-estate agency. All tenants share one MongoDB database; every document carries a tenantId . Isolation is enforced by code rather than by the database, so the code is written to fail loudly rather than quietly do the wrong thing. Never build a tenantId filter by hand. A global Mongoose plugin ( backend/tenancy/tenantPlugin.js ) adds it to every query, aggregation and write. Never add a bare unique: true . Uniqueness is per workspace: schema.index({ tenantId: 1, field: 1 }, { unique: true }) . A global unique lets whichever agency signed up first claim a slug or name for everyone. A query with no tenant context throws ( TenantScopeError ). This is deliberate; see the tenant context . Only three collections are global ( tenantScoped: false in their schema options): Tenant , Invoice and JobLock . The tenant plugin registerTenancy(mongoose) is called at the top of backend/index.js (and of every script, via scripts/_bootstrap.js ) before any model is imported . It also sets applyPluginsToChildSchemas to false : otherwise every embedded subdocument schema (voice notes on a listing, deals on a client, field definitions on a category) would get its own required tenantId and every write would fail with "branding.tenantId is required". What the plugin does to each schema: Operation Behaviour find , findOne , count , countDocuments , distinct , update* , delete* , findOneAnd* , replaceOne Injects tenantId into the filter. If the filter already names a different tenant, it throws instead of overriding. upserts Stamps tenantId with $setOnInsert , so a matched document never has its tenant rewritten. aggregate Puts the $match at the very front, before any $lookup or $group can widen it. Merges into a leading $match rather than unshifting (needed for $text , see listing search ) and casts the id to an ObjectId, since pipelines are not cast. save / create Stamps tenantId in a pre('validate') hook (validation runs as its own pre-save hook registered earlier, so stamping on save would be too late and every create would fail with "tenantId is required"). tenantId is immutable : a record never moves between agencies by accident. insertMany Stamps a copy of each element. Callers pass module-level constants (seed data, starter roles); mutating those made the first insert poison every later one with a stale tenant id. bulkWrite Mongoose fires no query middleware for it, so the plugin overrides the static and scopes each operation by hand. This is the fast path bulk import uses. estimatedDocumentCount Throws. It reads collection metadata with no filter, so it would report every tenant's rows. Use countDocuments() . A deliberate cross-tenant read on a model can also be written Model.acrossTenants('reason').find() , which requires a reason string. The tenant context backend/tenancy/tenantContext.js keeps the current tenant in Node's AsyncLocalStorage . The value is bound to one request's async chain, so two concurrent requests for two agencies cannot see each other's context (a module-level variable would not guarantee that). Function Use runWithTenant({ tenantId, tenant?, userId? }, fn) Run fn inside one workspace. Throws if given neither a tenantId nor an explicit bypass. withTenantBySlug(slug, fn) ( resolveTenant.js ) Same, looking the workspace up by slug. For scripts and non-request work. forEachTenant(fn, { serviceableOnly = true }) ( tenantContext.js ) Run fn(tenant) once in every workspace. One workspace failing does not stop the others (failures are collected). Skips suspended, cancelled and expired-trial workspaces unless serviceableOnly: false . This is what scheduled jobs use. runWithoutTenantScope('why', fn) Deliberately unscoped work: the platform console, migrations, the login lookup that must find a user before it knows the tenant. The reason string is mandatory and is recorded on the context so an audit can ask "which code paths run unscoped?". inHomeTenant(req, fn) Pin a lookup about the caller to their home workspace. See act-as . getTenantId() , getTenant() Read the active context ( null when unscoped). runWithTenant forces the callback's thenable to start executing while the context is still bound. A Mongoose query is lazy: await runWithTenant(store, () = Model.find()) would otherwise create the query inside the scope but execute it outside it, with no context at all. forEachTenant exists twice with different signatures. tenancy/tenantContext.js exports forEachTenant(fn, opts) , which the scheduler jobs use. tenancy/resolveTenant.js exports forEachTenant(reason, fn) , which iterates only trial and active workspaces and is used by server.js to seed default property types. Check the import path before using one. How a request picks its workspace resolveTenant() ( backend/tenancy/resolveTenant.js ) is mounted on /api after health and unsubscribe. It decides the tenant, then runs the rest of the request inside that tenant's context. Order, most authoritative first: The tid claim on the signed access_token cookie. Cannot be forged. A custom domain ( tenant.customDomain , e.g. crm.acme.in ). A subdomain of APP_DOMAIN ( acme. APP_DOMAIN ). Only a single label counts ( a.b. domain is not tenant "a.b"), and these are reserved and never treated as tenants: www app api admin auth static cdn assets localhost . The x-tenant header , a workspace slug. This is what the sign-in screen's Workspace field (web and mobile) and API clients send. The default tenant ( DEFAULT_TENANT_SLUG , default default ): single-workspace deployments, and the migration window before every session carried a tenant claim. Rules that follow from real bugs or abuse cases: Token and host must agree. If the token names one tenant and the host names another, the request is refused with a security log entry ( tenant_host_mismatch ). A valid session for one agency must not operate on another agency's domain. A named workspace that does not

title: Request pipeline and errors
text: Middleware order createApp() in backend/app.js is the one place the pipeline is assembled. The order is tested ( tests/requestPipeline.test.js ) because several of these steps only work in a particular sequence. # Middleware What it does and why it is here 0 trust proxy Set to 1 in production so req.ip is the client behind one proxy hop. 1 requestId First, so every later log line and every error body carries the id. See request ids . 2 securityHeaders Helmet with a CSP (self, Google Fonts, Cloudinary, data/blob images), HSTS one year with preload, no framing. 3 requestLogger On finish writes one structured access entry (method, url, status, duration, ip, user agent, user id); 5xx also to the error stream, 4xx as warnings. 4 express.json , express.urlencoded (10 MB), cookieParser The body is parsed before sanitising. See sanitising . 5 hpp HTTP parameter pollution: ?role=user role=admin collapses to one value. 6 mongoSanitization Strips Mongo operators from body, query and params; logs an injection attempt. allowDots: true . 7 xssProtection XSS-escapes query and params only , not the body. 8 compression , cors CORS from config.cors : production origins are FRONTEND_URL and ADMIN_URL ; development adds localhost:5173 and :3000 and EXTRA_CORS_ORIGINS . Credentials on. Allowed request headers include X-CSRF-Token and X-Request-Id . 9 morgan('dev') Development only. In production requestLogger is the single access log. 10 rate limiters If ENABLE_RATE_LIMITING is not false : strictRateLimit on /api/upload , then apiRateLimit on /api/ . See rate limits . 11 encryptResponse ( /api ) Optional AES-256-GCM envelope around JSON bodies when ENCRYPT_API_RESPONSES=true ; skips /api/health and /api/observability . On a crypto error it falls back to plaintext rather than breaking the response. 12 errorEnvelope Installed after encryptResponse on purpose: each wraps res.json and the last installed runs first, so code and requestId are added to the body before it is encrypted, not to the ciphertext envelope. 13 /api/health , /api/unsubscribe Answer before tenant resolution . A load-balancer probe has no workspace, and a broken tenant lookup must not take the pod out of service. The unsubscribe token names its own workspace, and a person's "stop" is honoured even for an agency since suspended or closed. 14 resolveTenant() ( /api ) Everything after this runs inside a tenant context. See Multi-tenancy . 15 readOnlyWhileActing Blocks non-GET requests during an operator's act-as session. See act-as . 16 requireCsrfToken Double-submit CSRF check on writes. See CSRF . 17 routers Tenant, share, platform, user, auth, listing, category and so on. Guards and validateBody live on the routes. 18 static, /uploads/docs , /uploads frontend/dist ; a 307 redirect from the old document URLs to /api/documents/file/:name ; listing photographs and avatars. 19 /api catch-all, then * Unknown /api path: JSON 404 NOT_FOUND (an HTML page if the client accepts text/html ). Anything else serves frontend/dist/index.html (or a development hint if there is no build). 20 globalErrorHandler Last. Every thrown error ends here. Request ids utils/requestContext.js gives each request an id. A caller-supplied X-Request-Id is kept if it matches ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,64}$ ; otherwise a UUID is generated. It is set on req.id , returned as the X-Request-Id response header, repeated as requestId in every error body, and stamped by the logger on every line written while the request is in flight (along with the tenant), so a "ref" a user reads out finds the log. getRequestId() works anywhere in the request's async chain. It is a separate AsyncLocalStorage from the tenant context on purpose: the id exists before the tenant is resolved (and for routes that have none), and the two must not be able to overwrite each other. Outside a request (jobs, scripts) it is null . One error shape Every failure answers: { "success": false, "statusCode": 409, "code": "VERSION_CONFLICT", // the contract - branch on this "message": "This record was changed by someone else while you were editing it.", "type": "conflict", // optional "field": "email", // optional "details": { "currentUpdatedAt": "..." }, // optional "requestId": "6f1c...", "timestamp": "2026-10-02T09:15:00.000Z", "path": "/api/listing/update/ id " } code is the contract; message is for a person. A client switching on "Category in use" broke the day the sentence was improved, and wording also changes with language. Codes are additive: older fields stay and code and requestId are added. How to raise an error Throw AppError ( new AppError(message, statusCode, isOperational = true, code?) ) or a subclass from utils/error.js : ValidationError (400, VALIDATION_FAILED , takes a field ), AuthenticationError (401), AuthorizationError (403), NotFoundError (404), ConflictError (409), VersionConflictError (409, VERSION_CONFLICT , takes details ), RateLimitError (429), DatabaseError (500). The legacy helper errorHandler(status, message) returns an AppError . Wrap async handlers in asyncHandler so a rejection reaches next(err) . A hand-written res.status(4xx).json({ success: false, ... }) still works: middleware/errorEnvelope.js adds code (from the status) and requestId to any success: false body with status = 400, leaving a code that is already present alone. About a hundred call sites (upload limits, the rate limiter, route guards) write errors themselves; rewriting each would be a hundred chances to change a message a client depends on. For a 409 the controller attaches details to say what the conflict is about (how many listings use the category, which fields still hold values). globalErrorHandler passes details through; dropping it once left the UI unable to offer the ?force=true choice. What classifyError does One pass turns any thrown value into { status, code, type, message, field, details } . (There used to be two passes that disagreed: the first mapped a bad ObjectId to 404 with type "validation", the second rewrote

title: Background jobs and automation
headings: Veto versus error: two different things
text: The scheduler backend/jobs/scheduler.js is deliberately dependency-free. Jobs here run every N minutes or once a day at a given hour, so a cron parser would buy expressiveness the app does not need and add a dependency to keep current. Before it existed there was no scheduler at all, which is why a set of schema fields never did anything: task.reminders[].sent , followUp.reminderSent , and tenant.trialEndsAt (only checked lazily, when somebody happened to make a request). Two properties matter: Single-firing across instances. The app ships under PM2 cluster mode and on hosts where more than one instance is normal. Each run takes a lease in Mongo ( models/jobLock.model.js : name unique, lockedUntil , owner , lastRunAt , lastResult ), so N instances still produce one run. It is a lease rather than a flag because a process can die mid-job: lockedUntil expires on its own, so a crash costs one cycle rather than wedging the job. JobLock is not tenant-scoped: the scheduler is infrastructure. Non-overlapping. A run that is still going holds its lease, so a slow job is skipped rather than stacked on itself. The in-process tick also refuses to overlap itself. How a job is claimed setInterval every 60 s (unref'd) → tick(now): for each job, one atomic findOneAndUpdate → lease free AND due? owner = this instance → run handler, renewing lease → release: lastRunAt = now, lockedUntil = epoch The decision is one atomic findOneAndUpdate with upsert . Read-then-write would let two instances both see a free lock and both take it. If two instances create the lock in the same instant, one gets a duplicate-key error (code 11000), which is treated as "lost the race", not as a failure. Due means: for dailyAt: 'HH:MM' (always UTC ), today's slot has passed and lastRunAt is before it; for everyMs , lastRunAt is at or before now - everyMs . Register with registerJob(name, { everyMs | dailyAt, leaseMs = 5 min }, handler) . The name is the lock key, so never rename one casually. dailyAt wins if both are given. Lease heartbeat. While a handler is running the lease is renewed every max(10 s, leaseMs / 3) . A fixed lease is a bet on how long a job takes, and the bet is wrong the moment the work grows: reminder jobs send email, mail costs seconds per message, and when the lease expired mid-run another instance claimed it and the same reminders went out twice. The lease stays short, so a process that dies still frees the job within one interval. A failing handler is logged, its lastResult is set to failed: message , and the lock is released; it does not crash the scheduler. tick(now) takes the time as an argument. Never read the clock inside a job's cadence logic. The cadence decision and the stored lastRunAt must agree on what time it is. Reading the clock inside made a daily job stamp wall-clock time while tick reasoned about the time it was given, so the two disagreed and the job never became due again. This is also what lets tests/scheduler.test.js drive the scheduler with a fake time. The registered jobs All jobs are registered in one place, backend/jobs/index.js ( registerAllJobs() , called once by startJobs() after the server is listening). Each job body runs inside forEachTenant() ( tenancy/tenantContext.js ), because a query with no tenant context throws by design: a sweep has to enter each workspace rather than querying across all of them. One workspace failing is recorded in the job's log line and does not stop the rest. Job (lock name) Cadence Lease What it does task-reminders every 5 min 5 min For tasks not done with a reminders[] entry due and unsent: marks it sent, then raises a task.due notification to the assignee. Up to 500 tasks per workspace per run. followup-reminders every 5 min 5 min For client follow-ups that are due, not completed and not yet reminded: marks reminderSent , notifies the lead's assignedTo with followup.due . Up to 500 clients per workspace per run. webhook-delivery every 60 s 2 min deliverDueWebhooks() : up to 50 due deliveries per workspace per run. See webhooks . sequence-steps every 15 min 10 min runDueSequenceSteps() : up to 100 due enrollments per workspace per run. See sequences . import-usage-reset daily 02:10 UTC 5 min Rolls the legacy tenant.importUsage counter into a new UTC month (all workspaces, including suspended: serviceableOnly: false ). See the note under imports . lead-rescore daily 03:00 UTC 15 min Recomputes score and temperature of open leads. See lead scoring . overdue-invoice-sweep daily 07:30 UTC 5 min Not per workspace (invoices are vendor-side): sets billing.state = 'past_due' on workspaces with an issued invoice past its due date. Only flags; never suspends. See Billing . trial-expiry-sweep daily 08:00 UTC 5 min Warns workspace admins with a system.alert notification when a trial has 7, 3 or 1 days left, and once it has lapsed (while within a day of the end). Includes workspaces that just became unserviceable. Reminders and webhooks are idempotent by construction: the reminder flag is set before the notification is sent ("if it fails we would rather drop one reminder than risk a loop that re-sends it every minute"), and webhook deliveries move to a terminal status. JOBS_ENABLED JOBS_ENABLED=false makes an instance serve traffic but take no leases (the scheduler is never started), useful when you want jobs confined to one host. Any other value, including unset, enables them. Because leases make firing single, you normally do not need this on a small cluster. On shutdown stopScheduler() clears the interval; note that a lease held by a run still in flight is not released by shutdown and simply expires. Lead scoring and temperature client.calculateScore() ( models/client.model.js ) is the only place the score is computed. It sums five factors and caps at 100 (the schema caps it too, so an over-100 total must not fail validation on a lead that is doing well): Factor Rule engagement 10 per communication in the last 30 days, max 30 budget 20 if budget.max 0 urgen

headings: The sidebar is data, not markup
text: Stack and layout React 18, Vite 4, Tailwind 3.3, react-router-dom 6, Redux Toolkit with redux-persist, i18next, Leaflet for maps, ApexCharts for charts, socket.io-client for realtime. Source lives in frontend/src : Folder What is in it app/ AppRoutes.jsx (the authoritative route list), AppShell.jsx , CrmShell.jsx , screenRegistry.js , commands.js (the shared command list), RouteSeo.jsx , keyboard shortcuts. pages/ One file per screen. Most are lazy-loaded from AppRoutes.jsx . components/ Feature components (panels in Settings, GlobalSearch , crm/* ). design-system/ Shared primitives, imported from the barrel '../design-system' . contexts/ TenantProvider , PermissionsContext , notifications, appearance, search. hooks/ useScreens , useCrmAccess , useActingAs , useListingForm , useColumnPrefs , utils/ http.js (API client), currency.js (all formatters), cloudinary.js , nativeFieldAliases.js , categoryFieldRules.js . i18n/ i18next setup and locales/*.json . redux/ Store and the user slice; only user is persisted. Routing and shells Two layouts. AppShell wraps public and seller routes with a minimal header. CrmShell wraps every CRM route with the sidebar and top bar and requires role === 'admin' || role === 'employee' . Guards are AdminRoute , SellerRoute , PrivateRoute and the canAccess check in CrmShell . Read frontend/src/app/AppRoutes.jsx rather than any list in prose. Renamed paths keep aliases: /contacts to /owners , /deals to /pipeline , /buyer-requirements to /buyers , /client-reports to /reports . Reachable without a session: / , the legal pages, /download , /sign-in , /forgot-password , /s/:token (a share link), /invite/:token and /unsubscribe/:token . The property book is not browsable anonymously. The sidebar is data, not markup The server owns what each screen is ( backend/tenancy/screenCatalogue.js : id, label, section, permission). The client owns how it looks ( app/screenRegistry.js : icon, route). hooks/useScreens.js intersects both with the workspace's feature flags and the user's permissions. Screen ids are a contract with every workspace's stored settings. Renaming one detaches the screen from the catalogue and it vanishes from the menu with no error. Add and deprecate freely; never rename. A workspace's own rename of a screen beats a translation ( useScreens compares label to defaultLabel ). Adding a screen: an entry in both files plus a route in AppRoutes.jsx . Command palette and shortcuts The K palette and the keyboard shortcuts read one list, app/commands.js ( useCommands ), filtered by screens and permissions. Add an action there, never in either consumer. A "New " command links to ?new=1 and the destination page opens its own create form. Talking to the API Always use apiClient from @/utils/http ; never raw fetch . import { apiClient, normalizeImageUrl } from '@/utils/http'; await apiClient.get('/endpoint'); await apiClient.post('/endpoint', data); await apiClient.patch('/endpoint', data); await apiClient.delete('/endpoint'); await apiClient.upload('/endpoint', formData); // multipart Sessions are httpOnly cookies. A 401 triggers one refresh and a retry ( fetchWithRefresh ); see Authentication . Failures arrive as one envelope with a code . Branch on code ; show message to people ( Request pipeline ). Pass { silent: true } to suppress the global error toast when the caller handles the failure itself (a widget that should degrade quietly). Run image URLs through normalizeImageUrl() ; it turns absolute localhost URLs into relative paths so production works. Uploads of images and voice notes go straight to Cloudinary from the browser ( utils/cloudinary.js , unsigned preset; audio uses the video resource type). Only documents go through /api/documents . Environment Variable Purpose VITE_API_URL API origin. Empty in dev; the Vite proxy forwards /api and /uploads to localhost:3000 . VITE_API_RESPONSE_SECRET Response decryption secret. VITE_SOCKET_URL Socket.IO endpoint. VITE_CLOUDINARY_CLOUD_NAME , VITE_CLOUDINARY_UPLOAD_PRESET Uploads. VITE_SITE_URL Public origin used for the sitemap, canonical URLs and social tags at build time. Defaults to https://realvista.duckdns.org . VITE_* values are baked in at build time, which is why production builds on the server that holds them. Design system Import from the barrel: import { Button, Modal, Table } from '../design-system' . Components: Avatar, Badge, Button, Card, ColumnToggle, Drawer, Dropdown, EmptyState, Input/Select/Textarea, KpiCard, Modal, PageHeader, Pagination, SearchBar, Skeleton, Spinner, Table, Tabs, Toggle (Switch/Checkbox), Toolbar, Tooltip. Modal and Drawer share useDialog . Icons: react-icons/hi (HeroIcons) only. No Font Awesome, no lucide, no emoji icons. Maps: Leaflet occupies z-index 400 800. On map pages use inline confirmation (a rose-50 strip with Cancel and Delete, see PropertyDocuments.jsx ) instead of a modal; elsewhere use ConfirmDialog . Tokens: new code should prefer theme tokens ( bg-card , border-border , text-foreground , text-muted-foreground , bg-secondary , hover:bg-accent ) over slate classes, so dark mode needs no override entry. Visual conventions Element Classes Page background bg-slate-50 Card bg-white border border-slate-200 rounded-xl p-5 shadow-sm Primary button bg-slate-900 hover:bg-slate-800 text-white rounded-lg Secondary button border border-slate-200 bg-white hover:bg-slate-50 rounded-lg CTA on dark bg-brand-600 hover:bg-brand-700 text-white Colour The accent is a deep petrol blue on an OKLCH ramp named brand in tailwind.config.js . The same config overrides Tailwind's stock indigo with that ramp, so the ~520 older indigo-* classes repaint coherently and the dark-mode override sheet in index.css keeps working. Use brand-* in new code; do not introduce new indigo-* . Interpolated class names never work. `text-${color}-400` is not emitted because Tailwind scans source as plain text. title: Authentication and sessions
headings: What every protected request goes through
text: The model in one minute Authentication is cookie-only . There is no bearer-token mode: the API never reads an Authorization header for identity, and the browser never holds a token in script-reachable storage. A sign-in sets three cookies; every later request carries them automatically. POST /api/auth/signin → access_token + refresh_token + csrf_token → 401? POST /api/auth/refresh → rotated pair, retry once The code lives in backend/controllers/auth.controller.js (issuing and rotating), backend/utils/verifyUser.js ( verifyToken , tryVerifyToken , requireAdmin , requireRole ), backend/middleware/csrf.js and backend/tenancy/resolveTenant.js . Cookies Cookie httpOnly Lifetime What it is access_token yes ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRY (default 15m ) plus a 1-minute buffer Signed JWT ( JWT_SECRET ). Proves the session. refresh_token yes REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRY (default 30d ) Signed JWT ( REFRESH_SECRET ). Only used to mint a new pair. csrf_token no, on purpose 30 days (fixed in middleware/csrf.js ) Random 32-byte value, base64url. A proof of same-origin, not an identity. Cookie lifetimes follow config. maxAge is derived from the same ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRY / REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRY that signs the JWT ( durationToMs accepts s , m , h , d ). A hard-coded 30-day cookie next to a 10-day token used to leave a stale cookie that outlived the token it carried and produced a confusing logout days later. The 1-minute buffer on the access cookie means the cookie always outlives its token. SameSite and Secure. In production all three cookies are SameSite=None; Secure so the app can be served from a different origin than the API. In development they are SameSite=Lax and not Secure . Clearing must match setting. A bare clearCookie('access_token') does not match a SameSite=None; Secure cookie, so the browser would keep it. clearSessionCookies() and the sign-out handlers clear each cookie with the same attributes it was set with. These three are also the only cookies listed on the public Cookie Policy ( pages/Legal.jsx ); the names and the "about 15 minutes / 30 days" lifetimes there agree with the code. JWT claims Both tokens carry the same claims and differ only in secret and expiry. Issuer and audience default to mern-estate-api and mern-estate-client ( JWT_ISSUER , JWT_AUDIENCE ) and are verified on every request. Claim Meaning id The user's id. tid The workspace the account lives in . Signed, so it cannot be forged by changing a host or header. resolveTenant prefers it over everything else. act Only on a platform operator's token while viewing a customer's workspace: the workspace being viewed . Ignored unless pa is also true . pa true only when startActingAs minted the token, after it re-read isPlatformAdmin from the database. iat , exp , iss , aud Standard. iat is compared with passwordChangedAt (see Passwords ). tid and act are never collapsed. Rewriting tid to the customer's workspace would put the operator's identity in a workspace their account is not in, and the session would stop resolving. Every query about the caller is pinned back to tid ( inHomeTenant / runWithTenant ); see Multi-tenancy . Signing in POST /api/auth/signin , rate limited ( authRateLimit , 20 per 15 minutes per IP by default), body validated by userValidation.login . curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/auth/signin \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'x-tenant: acme' \ -c cookies.txt \ -d '{"email":"owner@acme.in","password":"Secret@123"}' Success is 200 with the user document spread at the top level (no data wrapper; password and refreshTokens are removed), plus isPlatformAdmin so the console link can be shown to operators: { "success": true, "_id": "...", "email": "owner@acme.in", "role": "admin", "isPlatformAdmin": false, ... } and three Set-Cookie headers ( access_token , refresh_token , csrf_token ). The server also bumps lastLogin and loginCount , resets the failure counters and writes a SecurityLog row. Choosing the workspace Every agency shares one server address, so a person signing in has no session, host or token to tell the server which agency they belong to. The sign-in screen has a Workspace field; its value travels as the x-tenant header (web: stored in localStorage under rv.workspace by frontend/src/utils/workspace.js ; mobile: WorkspaceStore ). resolveTenant resolves, most authoritative first: the tid claim on a valid access token; a custom domain; a single-label subdomain of APP_DOMAIN (reserved: www app api admin auth static cdn assets localhost ); the x-tenant header; the default workspace ( DEFAULT_TENANT_SLUG , default default ). Two rules keep this safe: On entry routes the typed workspace beats an old cookie. POST /auth/signin , POST /user/password/request-otp , POST /user/password/reset and GET /tenant/lookup prefer the header over a session cookie left from another workspace. Otherwise signing in to B while holding A's cookie looked the email up in A and answered "invalid email or password". A typo is an answer, not a fallback. A named workspace that does not exist returns 404 with code: "WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND" instead of silently using the default, so nobody is signed in to another agency by mistake. { "success": false, "statusCode": 404, "code": "WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND", "message": "There's no workspace called \"acmee\". Check the name and try again.", "requestId": "..." } If a token names one workspace and the host names another, the request is refused ( tenant_host_mismatch is logged): a valid session for one agency must not operate on another agency's domain. Suspended, cancelled or expired-trial workspaces answer 403 with a plain-language reason. GET /api/tenant/lookup (rate limited, public) lets the sign-in screen confirm a name and show the workspace's logo before the password is typed. Failed attempts and lockout Wrong email or wrong password both answer 401 "Invalid email or password" , so the response does not say which half was wrong. The reason is recorded in the security log. title: Security and data protection
headings: Data rights, retention and the legal pages
text: How to read this page Everything here was checked against the code. Where a rule exists because of a bug that already happened, the bug is named, since the rule is easier to keep when the reason is known. The final section, What is not protected , is as important as the rest. Sign-in, cookies and CSRF are on their own page: Authentication and sessions . Tenant isolation All agencies share one database; every document carries a tenantId . Isolation is enforced by code, not by the database , in a global Mongoose plugin ( backend/tenancy/tenantPlugin.js , registered in index.js before any model is imported): A query with no tenant context throws . It does not silently run unscoped. A query that names a different tenant than the context throws. An operation the plugin cannot scope ( estimatedDocumentCount ) throws. Only the Tenant model is global. Everything else is scoped by existing, not by remembering to opt in. Deliberate cross-tenant work is spelled runWithoutTenantScope('why') and is greppable. Examples: opening a share link, accepting an invite, resolving which tenant a request belongs to. Uniqueness is { tenantId, field } ; a bare unique: true would let one agency's email block another's. Other places the boundary has to hold, all in code: Response caches. A cache sits in front of the database, so query scoping cannot protect it. getTenantScopedCache() ( utils/cache.js ) suffixes every key with the current tenant id (or none / unscoped ); plain getCache() is only for genuinely global data such as geocoding. The tenant record itself is cached in process for 60 seconds, so suspending a workspace takes effect within a minute. Sockets. Rooms are tenant: id and user: id . A bare io.emit() reaches every agency, so controllers use emitToTenant() / emitToUser() only. A message:send to a user id from another workspace is refused ("That person is not in this workspace.") because the recipient lookup runs in the sender's tenant. Presence lists and typing pings are scoped the same way. Scripts, jobs and socket handlers must enter a tenant explicitly ( runWithTenant , withTenantBySlug , forEachTenant ). CLI scripts load models through scripts/_bootstrap.js ; a hoisted import of a model compiles its schema before the plugin and writes records with no tenantId that the app can never see. Platform vs workspace admin. role: 'admin' administers one agency. isPlatformAdmin is a separate, select: false flag that guards /api/platform/* and the log-query endpoints. requirePlatformAdmin re-reads it from the database on each call and never trusts the token. See Multi-tenancy . Who can reach what Every mounted route is guarded or declared public. backend/security/publicRoutes.js lists the endpoints that are public on purpose, each with a reason. tests/routeAccess.test.js walks the live Express router and fails the build for any route that is neither guarded ( verifyToken , tryVerifyToken , requireAdmin , requirePermission , requirePlatformAdmin , canCreateListing ) nor listed. If it fails, add the missing guard; do not add the route to the allowlist. The CSRF exemptions are derived from the same list. Permissions come from one catalogue. utils/permissionCatalogue.js (35 permissions) generates the role schema, and requirePermission() throws at module load on an unknown key. tests/permissionCatalogue.test.js walks the route files. This exists because one route asked for manage_settings , which was never a permission, so every non-admin was denied forever. See Team, roles and permissions . The property book is not public. Nothing about a listing, category or property type is reachable without a session. Sharing outside the agency goes through share links (below). Object-level checks. Single-item handlers check ownership or staff status. A 2026-08 review found one missing check ( GET /api/buyer-requirements/:id , an IDOR); buyerRequirement.controller.js now applies one isStaff(user) helper (admin and employee are org-wide) consistently across its single-item handlers. Documents are not public. Files under /uploads/docs/ redirect (307) to /api/documents/file/:filename , which goes through verifyToken and the ownership check, and responds with X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and Content-Disposition: attachment so a document never renders inside the app's origin. Validation and injection Every POST/PUT/PATCH needs validateBody(schema) . It runs Joi with abortEarly and stripUnknown: true and replaces req.body with the cleaned value. tests/validationCoverage.test.js fails a new write route that has none unless it is allowlisted with a reason. Because unknown fields are dropped, a field the controller reads but the schema omits is silently lost, which is also what blocks mass assignment (for example, nobody can send isPlatformAdmin or tenantId ). Operator injection. The body is parsed before express-mongo-sanitize runs ( $ne , $where and similar keys are replaced with _ , logged as an injection attempt). Earlier, sanitizing ran while req.body was still undefined, so {"email":{"$ne":null}} reached controllers. Dotted keys are allowed ( allowDots ) because an import's column mapping is keyed by header text like "Phone no.". hpp collapses duplicate query parameters ( ?role=user role=admin ). tests/requestPipeline.test.js pins this order. XSS on input. The xss rewrite is applied to query and params only . Bodies legitimately carry markup (email templates up to 100 KB, notes such as " 3 BHK") and escaping on the way in would corrupt what the user saved. Escaping is done on output: React escapes what it renders, mail templates render through utils/emailTemplates.js , and the API's 404 page escapes the URL it echoes. Regexes. User text never goes into a regex raw: use utils/escapeRegex.js ( containsInsensitive , equalsInsensitive ), which also coerces query objects to strings. Category field patterns are screened for ReDoS-prone shapes ( utils/categoryFields.js ). Paging and sorting are clamped ( limit max 500) and sort keys
