headings: Worked example: sign in, then create a lead
text: Base URL and transport All routes are under /api . The API and the built web app are served by the same Express process in production ( frontend/dist ), so the web app is same-origin. In development the Vite server on port 5173 proxies /api and /uploads to localhost:3000 ( frontend/vite.config.js ), so VITE_API_URL is empty. A split deployment sets VITE_API_URL and must list the app's origin in FRONTEND_URL / ADMIN_URL / EXTRA_CORS_ORIGINS . Bodies are JSON ( Content-Type: application/json , 10 MB limit) except uploads ( multipart/form-data ). Responses are JSON and gzip-compressed. The generated, always-current endpoint reference is under API reference . It is built from the live router and the same Joi schemas that validate requests ( backend/utils/openapi.js ), so it cannot drift; never hand-edit docs/openapi.json . A workspace admin can also fetch it from a running server at GET /api/docs/openapi.json , or regenerate the file with npm run docs:openapi in backend/ . Headers a client sends Header or cookie When Notes Cookie: access_token, refresh_token, csrf_token Every authenticated call Set by sign-in. There is no Authorization: Bearer mode. Details: Authentication and sessions . X-CSRF-Token Every POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE made with a session Must equal the csrf_token cookie. Otherwise 403 CSRF_TOKEN_INVALID or CSRF_COOKIE_MISSING . Get it from the cookie or GET /api/auth/csrf . x-tenant: workspace-slug Sign-in, password reset, tenant lookup (and any call with no session) Which agency. Once signed in, the token's tid wins and the header is ignored. Unknown slug: 404 WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND . X-Request-Id Optional Kept if it matches ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,64}$ , else replaced with a UUID. x-share-passcode Opening a passcode-protected share link Also accepted as ?passcode= . Success responses There is no single success envelope . Three shapes exist; check the reference for the endpoint you call. Helper envelope ( sendSuccessResponse ): { "success": true, "statusCode": 200, "message": "...", "data": ..., "timestamp": "ISO" } . Used by tenant, platform, share, invite, health and most newer controllers. Hand-written : { "success": true, "data": ... } , and for lists { "success": true, "data": [...], "page": 1, "limit": 20, "total": 134 } (e.g. GET /api/clients , POST /api/clients answers 201 { success, data } ). Top-level fields : sign-in and refresh spread the user document next to success ; uploads answer { success, url } or { success, urls } . In every shape a boolean success is present, and failures always use the error envelope below. Errors Every failure answers one shape. code is the contract; message is for a person and may be reworded or translated. Branch on code . { "success": false, "statusCode": 409, "code": "VERSION_CONFLICT", "message": "This record was changed by someone else while you were editing it.", "type": "conflict", "details": { "currentUpdatedAt": "2026-10-01T09:12:44.000Z" }, "requestId": "6c1f0f63-6a63-4d0b-9d0c-2f3d8e1a5b77", "timestamp": "2026-10-01T09:13:02.114Z", "path": "/api/clients/65f..." } Optional fields: type ( validation , authentication , authorization , not_found , conflict , rate_limit , database ), field (the offending input), details . Hand-written res.status(4xx).json({ success:false, ... }) responses still get code and requestId added by middleware/errorEnvelope.js . Quote requestId (also in the X-Request-Id response header) in a bug report; the logger stamps it on every line. In production an unexpected 500 returns a generic sentence and the request id, never the internal message. Codes Code Status Meaning VALIDATION_FAILED 400 Joi or model validation. field names the input; only the first problem is reported. BAD_REQUEST 400, 413 Malformed JSON, body too large, other 400s. INVALID_ID 404 An id that is not an ObjectId. Answered as 404 on purpose: to a person following a link, a malformed id and a missing record are the same thing. UNAUTHENTICATED 401 No usable session. The web client tries /auth/refresh once. SESSION_EXPIRED 401 An expired JWT reached the error handler. FORBIDDEN 403 Signed in but not allowed (role, permission, read-only acting session, disabled or suspended workspace). NOT_FOUND 404 No such record or route. CONFLICT 409 Generic conflict, e.g. a duplicate lead. DUPLICATE 409 A unique index fired (the message names the field, never the tenant). VERSION_CONFLICT 409 See Edit conflicts . PLAN_LIMIT 402 The workspace's plan does not cover this. See Plan limits . RATE_LIMITED 429 Too many requests. INTERNAL 5xx Unexpected error. Endpoint-specific codes, all set by the code that raises them: CSRF_TOKEN_INVALID , CSRF_COOKIE_MISSING (403), WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND (404), INVITE_REPLACED (410). Some responses add their own flags next to code : a share link answers passcodeRequired: true with 401, and an expired link 410 with expired: true . A CastError and a duplicate-key error are translated for you: a bad id is 404 INVALID_ID ; E11000 is 409 DUPLICATE with a message like "Email already exists". Sign-in failures are intentionally uniform ( 401 "Invalid email or password"). Paging, sorting and filtering Query : ?page=1 limit=20 sort=field:asc|desc . utils/listQuery.js turns untrusted values into safe numbers: non-numeric or non-positive page / limit fall back to defaults (page 1, limit 20 unless the endpoint sets another), and limit is capped at 500 . sort is an allowlist per endpoint ; anything else falls back to the endpoint's default, with _id always the final tie-breaker so rows do not repeat or vanish across pages. Response : { success, data: [...], page, limit, total } . Sorting and paging happen in the database, so sort by the server ( sort= ), never by re-sorting one page. Bare arrays when page is absent. GET /api/owner/list and GET /api/buyer-requirements page only when page is passed; without it they return a bare array, which the mobile app and the listing form read. Do not assume a list is wrapped. Clients list sorts by name, score, temper

title: Deploy and operate
headings: One-time: drop the old user TTL index
text: What runs where One Node process ( backend/index.js ) serves the API on /api , Socket.IO, uploaded files on /uploads and, when frontend/dist exists, the built web app with an SPA fallback. MongoDB is the only required dependency. Redis, SMTP, Twilio, Cloudinary and OpenObserve are optional and degrade gracefully ( table below ). The frontend's VITE_* values are compiled into the bundle, so they are fixed at build time, not read at runtime. Browser / app → nginx or platform router → Node :3000 (API, sockets, /uploads) → MongoDB Backend environment variables Read from backend/.env (loaded by config/environment.js via dotenv) or the real environment. The process exits at boot if one of the five required variables is missing; validateConfig() adds the production checks noted below. Only variables read by code are listed; backend/.env.example also carries names nothing reads (see Stale files ). Required and core Variable Default Purpose NODE_ENV required development , production or test . Production: SameSite=None; Secure cookies, CORS limited to FRONTEND_URL / ADMIN_URL , trust proxy = 1, no stack traces, config validation. MONGO_URI required Connection string. Production rejects an unset value or the old local default. JWT_SECRET required Access-token key, at least 32 characters; the placeholder dev_secret is refused in production. REFRESH_SECRET required Refresh-token key, at least 32 characters. Keep it different from JWT_SECRET . Rotating either signs everyone out. MESSAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY required Chat-at-rest key (AES-256-GCM via scrypt). Changing it makes existing messages undecryptable, so treat it like a database key. PORT / HOST 3000 / 0.0.0.0 Listen address. Render's blueprint sets PORT=10000 . FRONTEND_URL none Production CORS origin and the base of links in emails (fallback when a workspace has no domain). Missing in production prints a warning, not an exit. ADMIN_URL none Second production CORS origin. EXTRA_CORS_ORIGINS none Comma-separated extra origins; development only (ignored in production). Tenancy Variable Default Purpose APP_DOMAIN empty Enables subdomain routing: acme. APP_DOMAIN resolves to workspace slug acme . DEFAULT_TENANT_SLUG default Fallback workspace for single-workspace deployments and un-migrated tokens. Production requires APP_DOMAIN or DEFAULT_TENANT_SLUG to be set explicitly (checked on the raw environment, since the config value always has the default fallback); otherwise the process exits. PUBLIC_API_URL falls back to the workspace base URL Only for a split deployment: the API's public base, used in one-click unsubscribe links. PUBLIC_BASE_URL empty Base for the property link appended to chat messages that reference a listing. Auth and limits Variable Default Purpose ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRY / REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRY 15m / 30d Also drive the cookie lifetimes. JWT_ISSUER / JWT_AUDIENCE mern-estate-api / mern-estate-client Verified on every token. MAX_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS 5 Failures before lockout. LOCKOUT_DURATION 900000 Lockout in milliseconds. ENABLE_RATE_LIMITING on Set to false to disable the app-level /api and /api/upload limiters (per-route auth limiters stay). RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS 900000 Window for the general and auth limiters. RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS 1000 General limit per window. AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX 20 Credential endpoints per window; refresh allows max(this x 5, 500). STRICT_RATE_LIMIT_MAX 30 Uploads per minute. UNSUBSCRIBE_SECRET derived from JWT_SECRET Signs unsubscribe links. Set once, never rotate. API_RESPONSE_SECRET + ENCRYPT_API_RESPONSES=true off AES-GCM response encryption; the frontend needs the matching VITE_API_RESPONSE_SECRET at build. See API conventions . Database, cache and scaling Variable Default Purpose DB_MAX_POOL_SIZE 10 Mongo connection pool. DB_SERVER_SELECTION_TIMEOUT 5000 ms. DB_SOCKET_TIMEOUT 45000 ms. CACHE_TTL / CACHE_MAX_SIZE 300 / 100 In-process response cache, seconds / entries. REDIS_URL unset Shares the rate limiter and cache invalidation across instances (see Scaling ). Redis down does not fail readiness. JOBS_ENABLED on false = serve traffic but take no scheduler leases. SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS 10000 Grace period before open connections are closed on SIGTERM. Mail, SMS and observability Variable Default Purpose SMTP_HOST smtp.gmail.com in the mailer Platform SMTP. A transport is built only if SMTP_USER and SMTP_PASS are both set. A workspace can configure its own SMTP under Settings; its password is stored encrypted and never returned. SMTP_PORT 587 TLS-on-connect is used only when the port is 465 . SMTP_USER / SMTP_PASS none Credentials. SMTP_FROM falls back to SMTP_USER Sender address (the variable the code reads; see Stale files ). TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID / TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN / TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER none Optional SMS. OPENOBSERVE_URL http://localhost:5080 Log shipping and the platform console's log query. OPENOBSERVE_ORG default OPENOBSERVE_USERNAME / OPENOBSERVE_PASSWORD none Shipping is gated on these. Unset: logs go to stdout and everything else is dropped (production prints a warning at boot). LOG_LEVEL info error , warn , info , debug . CLOUDINARY_CLOUD_NAME none Only read by the system-status report ( controllers/systemStatus.controller.js , admin-only GET /api/metrics/system ) to say whether uploads look configured; it also accepts VITE_CLOUDINARY_CLOUD_NAME . Uploads themselves are made by the browser. METRICS_TOKEN unset If set, /api/health/metrics requires Authorization: Bearer token ; unset leaves it open. Scripts only Variable Used by Purpose BACKUP_DIR backup, restore Default repo /backups . BACKUP_RETENTION_COUNT backup; compose backup service Default 7 . ALLOW_PRODUCTION_RESTORE restore Must be true to restore when NODE_ENV=production . LOG_RETENTION_DAYS , COMPRESS_LOGS npm run logs:rotate Default 30 days; gzip when true . Frontend build variables Variable Purpose VITE_API_URL API origin; empty in development (proxy) and for same-origin production. VITE_SOCKET_URL Socket origin; empty uses same origin. VITE_CLOUDINARY

headings: Pointing the app at a backend
RELEASE.md: what is done, what is left
text: What it is mobile/ is a separate Flutter project ( realvista_crm , version 1.0.4+5 in pubspec.yaml ) that talks to the same backend as the web app. There is no mobile-specific API and no push-notification service: real-time updates come over Socket.IO while the app is open. The Android build is distributed as a sideloaded APK from the web app's /download page; it is not on the Play Store, and nothing in the repository shows an iOS build having been produced (Xcode is needed and the release notes list iOS signing as still to do). Item Value Application id / bundle id com.realvista.realvista_crm ; display name "Real Vista" SDK Flutter 3.24.5 (Dart ^3.5.3 ), Gradle 8.3, AGP 8.1.0, Kotlin 1.8.22, compileSdk 35 State and routing flutter_riverpod , go_router Networking dio + cookie_jar / dio_cookie_manager , socket_io_client Other flutter_map (OpenStreetMap tiles, as the web Leaflet map), cached_network_image , file_picker , image_picker , url_launcher , share_plus , connectivity_plus Which Flutter to use Use Flutter 3.24.5, not a newer one. Current Flutter's Gradle plugin needs Gradle 8.14 or newer, and --android-skip-build-dependency-validation does not rescue it: the build fails later inside AGP 8.1.0. Closing that gap is an Android toolchain migration across all plugin dependencies, not a version bump. Running a newer flutter against this project also rewrites android/gradle.properties , analysis_options.yaml and pubspec.lock in place; check git status afterwards and revert if you did not mean to migrate ( mobile/RELEASE.md ). A working Android build environment needs the SDK path and a JDK that Gradle 8.3 can use (JDK 17; the newest JDK is too new). Example, adjusting paths to your machine: export PATH="$HOME/sdks/flutter-3.24.5/bin:$PATH" export ANDROID_HOME=/opt/homebrew/share/android-commandlinetools export ANDROID_SDK_ROOT="$ANDROID_HOME" export JAVA_HOME=$(/usr/libexec/java_home -v 17) Code layout Path under mobile/lib Contents main.dart Disables runtime font fetching, creates the ApiClient from Env.apiBaseUrl , overrides apiClientProvider , mounts MaterialApp.router inside RealtimeOverlay . core/config/env.dart API base URL (below). core/network/ api_client.dart (Dio, cookie jar, interceptors), workspace_store.dart , providers.dart . core/realtime/ SocketService (connect once per session). core/theme/ , shared/widgets/ Design tokens ported from the web Tailwind config and widgets mirroring the web design system (button, badge, card, KPI card, text and dropdown fields, states). app/router/ app_router.dart (guards), bottom-nav shell, quick-action sheet, "More" screen. features/* auth , dashboard , leads , properties , listing_form , owners , buyers , tasks , activities , transactions , messages , notifications , documents , reports , analytics , profile , settings , admin , legal , permissions . Each has data/ (API wrapper), domain/ (models) and presentation/ . The shell has four bottom tabs (Home, Leads, Properties, Activities), a centre quick-action button and an overflow "More" screen, pruned by the user's permissions the way the web sidebar is ( canProvider mirrors PermissionsContext.jsx : admins short-circuit to all, employees fetch their permission map, other roles get none). Every API wrapper converts a DioException into an AppFailure so UI code never inspects status codes. How it authenticates The mobile app has no token handling of its own . It uses exactly the cookie protocol the browser uses ( Authentication and sessions ); the only differences are where the cookies live and how the CSRF token is obtained. Cookie storage. On native platforms ApiClient.create builds a PersistCookieJar backed by files under the app-support directory ( .cookies/ ), attached through Dio's CookieManager , so the 30-day session survives app restarts. On Flutter web there is no dart:io ; the browser stores and sends the cookies and the adapter is only told withCredentials = true . Workspace. WorkspaceStore keeps the chosen workspace slug (file workspace.txt ; memory only on web) and an interceptor sends it as x-tenant on every request unless the call names one itself (the login screen checks a typed name via GET /api/tenant/lookup with an explicit header). Normalised to lower case, letters, digits and dashes, the same rule as the web's utils/workspace.js . A session carries its own workspace and the server trusts that over the header, so it only decides where sign-in and "forgot password" look. Sign in. POST /api/auth/signin with email and password; the response user becomes the auth state. At launch AuthController.bootstrap() calls GET /api/user/me : an authentication failure means signed out; any other failure shows an "Unable to reach Real Vista" screen with a retry rather than a login form. Refresh. A 401 on any non-auth call triggers one POST /api/auth/refresh (concurrent 401s share one in-flight call, because the backend treats a re-presented refresh token as theft and wipes every session) and the original request is replayed once. Sign-in, refresh and signup paths are never retried. CSRF. A Flutter web build cannot read document.cookie , so instead of reading the cookie the interceptor asks the server: GET /api/auth/csrf returns the value the jar or browser just sent. It is cached, attached as X-CSRF-Token to every non-GET call except the unauthenticated writes (sign-in, signup, refresh, csrf, password OTP and reset), and refetched once on 403 CSRF_TOKEN_INVALID (the token rotates on refresh and act-as). Sign out. POST /api/auth/signout , plus signout-all on request, then clearSession() deletes the jar so a stale refresh cookie does not linger. On web clearing is a no-op; the server's Set-Cookie expires the cookies. Terms gate. After sign-in the app asks the backend whether the current Terms version still needs accepting. text: Each answer names the code that produces the symptom, so you can confirm the cause rather than guess. When you report a problem, quote the requestId from the error body (also the X-Request-Id response header): it finds the exact request in the logs. Setup and development The backend crashes on start with a SlowBuffer error. You are on Node 25. It removed SlowBuffer , which the jsonwebtoken dependency chain ( jwa , buffer-equal-constant-time ) still uses. Run the backend on Node 20; CI does ( .github/workflows/ci.yml ). With Homebrew: PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/node@20/bin:$PATH" npm run dev . The Vite frontend runs fine on newer Node. The backend exits immediately saying environment variables are missing, or configuration validation failed. config/environment.js exits if any of JWT_SECRET , REFRESH_SECRET , MONGO_URI , NODE_ENV , MESSAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY is unset. validateConfig() then requires both JWT secrets to be at least 32 characters and, in production, either APP_DOMAIN or DEFAULT_TENANT_SLUG . The last one catches a quiet failure: with neither, requests fall back to a workspace slugged default that may not exist, and because a query with no workspace throws, the whole API would be down rather than degraded. See the variable table . MongoDB will not connect locally. Check the server is actually listening ( lsof -nP -iTCP:27017 -sTCP:LISTEN ). On macOS mongod --fork is unsupported; start it with mongod --config /opt/homebrew/etc/mongod.conf in a background shell. An Atlas mongodb+srv:// URI whose cluster was deleted fails DNS resolution; point MONGO_URI at a local database instead. npm install fails with 401 on package fetches. A user-level ~/.npmrc points at a private registry. Override per command: npm_config_registry=https://registry.npmjs.org npm install . Separately, the frontend's xlsx dependency resolves to a tarball on cdn.sheetjs.com , so installs (and CI) need egress to it; install with --legacy-peer-deps . The Flutter web app (or a second frontend origin) says "Unable to reach Real Vista" and nothing loads. The browser is blocking the call under CORS. In development only the Vite and API origins are allowed by default; add the extra origin, comma-separated, to EXTRA_CORS_ORIGINS in backend/.env (for example http://localhost:54321 ). In production the allowed origins are only FRONTEND_URL and ADMIN_URL ; EXTRA_CORS_ORIGINS is ignored there. A native mobile app sends no Origin and is not affected. A seed or one-off script ran, but the records are invisible in the app. The script imported a model directly. Tenant scoping is a global Mongoose plugin and only applies to schemas compiled after it is registered; a hoisted import compiles the schema first, so the records are written with no tenantId and the app can never see them. Load models with const { models, inWorkspace, close } = await bootstrapScript() from scripts/_bootstrap.js . It takes --workspace slug and refuses to guess when several workspaces exist. Records already written without a tenantId have to be repaired by hand ( npm run db:migrate-tenancy stamps documents that have none, but it is a one-time migration; read it first). An error says "a query ran with no tenant context". That is the isolation guarantee working. tenantPlugin.js throws rather than run an unscoped query. In a request it means something ran outside the tenant context (for example work started after the response, or a callback that lost async context). In a script, cron job or socket handler, enter a workspace explicitly with runWithTenant , withTenantBySlug or forEachTenant . For deliberate cross-tenant work use runWithoutTenantScope('why') , and never build a tenantId filter by hand. A related error says a query asked for a different tenant than the request's; that is also deliberate. My test calls a controller directly and gets an empty response with no error. asyncHandler does not return its promise, so await controller(req, res, next) resolves before any database work finishes. Either go through HTTP with supertest (which needs a session), or call the handler without awaiting and poll until res.body is set or next fires. Creating a second user without a phone number fails with a duplicate key error. An obsolete unique index survived. Mongoose never drops an index it no longer declares, so the old phone_1 (plain unique and sparse, which still collides on null ) outlives the model's partial index tenant_phone_unique_string . The same class of problem is why db:migrate-tenancy drops the old global unique indexes (a leftover email_1 makes the second agency's duplicate email fail). Drop the stale index ( db.users.dropIndex('phone_1') ) or run User.syncIndexes() once. I ran db:seed-fresh and lost data. It is destructive with no confirmation prompt: it wipes the collections of the workspace it runs in and reseeds sample data (keeping the first admin). Only use it on a throwaway database. To empty a real workspace safely, scripts/purgeWorkspaceData.js --workspace slug --confirm writes a JSON backup first and keeps the tenant, admins and roles. Sign-in and sessions Sign-in says "invalid email or password", but the credentials are right. Usually the wrong workspace. The same email can exist in two agencies, and an unauthenticated request with no workspace falls back to DEFAULT_TENANT_SLUG . Enter the workspace name on the sign-in screen (sent as x-tenant ). A name that does not exist answers 404 WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND ("There's no workspace called ...") instead of using the default. If the account is locked the message says so: "Account locked. Try again in N minute(s)". Five wrong passwords ( MAX_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS ) lock the account for 15 minutes ( LOCKOUT_DURATION ), and the lock is checked before the password, so the right password does not help until it lapses. Every request returns 401 and the app keeps sending me back to sign-in. Work down this list. Cookies not stored. In production the cookies are SameSite=None; Secure , so the site must be served over
